title: Obstructions and Constructive Repairs for Shifted Dimensional MATBG Schemes on Deleted Knodel Graphs
abstract: We analyze the minimum average time broadcast graph (MATBG) construction on deleted Knodel graphs KG'(n-1) proposed in Section 5 of Altay, Fakharan, and Harutyunyan (arXiv:2611.34167v1) and prove both three infinite-family obstructions to their shifted dimensional scheme and three constructive repairs. First, Theorem A shows that shifted dimensional schedules suffer round-i vertex collisions in KG(n) whenever n <= n_max(k,i) = 2^k - 2^i - 4, with asymptotic half-loss 2^{k-2} - 2 at (n,i) = (2^{k-1}+2, 1), proving the Section 5 MATBG claim unproved on intermediate orders n in [2^{k-1}+2, 2^k - 6]. Second, Theorem B proves that for antipodal originators u = n/2 with n = 4m, all 2(k-1) standard and reverse cyclic shifts hit the deleted vertex 0 before round k. Third, Theorem C exhibits a first-half shortcut collision w = 2^{k-2} - 1 in I_{k-1}. Positively, Theorem D provides a universal single-edge shortcut reroute (2^{k-1}-1 -> 2^{k-2}-1) closing Sub-case 5 across the open second half [3*2^{k-2}, 2^k-2], Theorem E establishes a 2-adic shift s = 1 + v_2((n - 2^{k-1})/2) for u = 2^{k-2}, and Theorem F yields the first complete, gap-free MATBG proof for KG'(2^k - 5) and KG'(2^k - 3) for all k >= 4. All 24 universal modular-arithmetic theorems are formally verified in Lean 4.35.0 (0 sorry, 0 custom axioms, 0 Classical.choice, 0 warnings), accompanied by an AST-audited zero-float Python verifier, 16 JSON certificates (C01-C16), and 48 unit and forgery-rejection tests.
